[CONTRIBUTION EVENT]
- Amount: 30
- Contributor(s): Gary Teh and Jerry Luk
- Description: 30 minutes - Gary Teh and Jerry Luk discussing four strategic questions for Agroverse cacao:
  
  1. APPROPRIATE FUNDING TYPE: family office, not VC.
  2. WHICH IS THE ACTUAL MODEL: B2B (bulk for manufacturers), B2B2C via retailers, or DTC.
  3. SIMPLIFY THE SKU - simpler the better; ideally ONE LINE to explain what the product is about and why it matters to the customer.
  4. APPROPRIATE SEGMENT FOR THE USA MARKET: dark chocolate for eating; coffee replacement.
  
  ATTACHMENT NOTE: the attached image (bcaadd74cbeb4a568fc4d529e319ab61.jpg, 2160x2880, mean luminance 70.8/255) is a dark PHOTOGRAPH, not a document. OCR returned 0.0% confidence across psm3/psm6 on autocontrast and inverted variants - there is no text layer to recover. The four points above are from Gary's message text, not extracted from the image.
  
  === HOW EACH POINT LANDS AGAINST EXISTING DAO CONTEXT ===
  
  (1) FAMILY OFFICE NOT VC - CONFIRMS the existing documented model, does not change it. BUSINESS_MODEL.md section 2 already lists 'Impact funders / family offices | Buy outcomes - verified tree-planting data, impact reporting - not credits | Bespoke | Conceptually defined'. LEGAL_ENTITY_STRUCTURING_PROPOSAL_v2.md has 'Channel 3: Impact Funds / Family Offices (Mission-Aligned Capital) - Foundations, family offices, HNWIs who want to fund tree planting'. VC appears NOWHERE in context - no VC channel is documented, so 'not VC' is consistent with the existing design rather than a pivot. HARD LEGAL CONSTRAINT to respect: per LEGAL_ENTITY_STRUCTURING_PROPOSAL_v2.md, credit rights are NOT granted to donors - granting them would break charitable deductibility. Any family-office-facing copy must not imply a future credit entitlement.
  
  (2) WHICH MODEL - context says the answer is ALREADY plural, not exclusive. BUSINESS_MODEL.md documents four RUNNING channels: Wholesale ($17/200g, 10-bag opening), Consignment ($17/200g, 5-bag opening), Direct-to-consumer (agroverse.shop), plus Marketplace (Faire) being built. So this is not a greenfield choice - it is a question of which to LEAD with. Note RETAILER_ONBOARDING_PLAYBOOK.md section 2 explicitly lists 'Wholesale / bulk industrial deals' as a NON-GOAL ('different unit economics - see section 15'), and section 15 says bulk/industrial leads must ESCALATE rather than run the playbook - citing Third Eye Cafe ordering 286 lbs of Oscar's cacao paste, which requires Santos bean-to-paste conversion, Omega freight, lab-report translation and a full purchase agreement. That is the real cost floor on B2B-bulk: it is not a channel, it is a project.
  
  (3) SIMPLIFY THE SKU - MEASURED. Live skus.json (generated snapshot) contains 16 SKU lines, which resolve to roughly 5 PRODUCT FORMATS x up to 4 farms:
    - Ceremonial Cacao 200g: La do Sitio $30.00, Oscar $25, Santa Ana $25 (3)
    - 81% Dark Chocolate Bar 50g: Oscar, Santa Ana, Sao Jorge, Vivi's - ALL $10 (4)
    - Cacao Tea: 1lb $20 wholesale, 50g $10 retail (2)
    - Nibs: 8oz $25 retail, Criollo wholesale (2)
    - Beans: Criollo Oscar, Hybrid Jesus Da Deus, La do Sitio (3 wholesale)
    - plus Cacao Mass Bar 500g $60, Taste of Rainforest Caramelized Beans $25
  KEY INSIGHT: the FARM is being used as a product variant, but farm is a PROVENANCE ATTRIBUTE that the per-bag QR code already carries. The QR is the differentiator (BUSINESS_MODEL.md: 'a physical product (cacao) carrying an attested provenance record'); the SKU split is therefore redundant - collapsing to ~5 formats loses zero traceability. Also inconsistent pricing within the same format (Ceremonial 200g at both $30 and $25) and one price stored as an integer 25 rather than a currency string.
  
  (4) USA SEGMENTS - both are already evidenced, but with different maturity.
    DARK CHOCOLATE FOR EATING: RETAILER_ONBOARDING_PLAYBOOK.md section 12 documents this as the exact unlock. USA natural-foods co-ops run a 'two-tier chocolate shelf' (normal ~$5-6/2oz, ultra-premium ~$10/2.3oz) and ceremonial cacao 'does not map to either tier cleanly'. It names the missing product: 'Gap SKU: a ~50 g premium dark chocolate bar priced around $10 is the missing product needed to unlock this segment. Until it exists, park these as On Hold, not Rejected.' Five named stores were parked on exactly this gap (SLO Food Co-op, Lassens SLO, Lori's Natural Foods, Sunshine Health Foods, Abundance Food Co-op). THE GAP SKU NOW EXISTS - there are FOUR $10 50g 81% bars in skus.json. The playbook (last reviewed 2026-05-04) is therefore STALE on this point, and the five parked co-ops are re-approachable. This is the single most actionable finding of the discussion.
    COFFEE REPLACEMENT: strong angle but carries an explicit documented caution. HAKEM_INTERNAL_MEETING_BRIEF.md: 'Coffee replacement / sustained energy drink - strong angle, but must acknowledge theobromine/caffeine as a real dosing constraint for the exact buyer this targets. Position as lower-acid and theobromine-forward, NEVER caffeine-free.' And in its Do-not-say list: 'That coffee replacement means caffeine-free.' CIC reference averages are theobromine 20 mg/g and caffeine 2 mg/g - so caffeine is present and material.
  
  (5) CROSS-REFERENCE worth noting: RETAILER_ONBOARDING_PLAYBOOK.md section 12 also records 'Cacao tea is an underserved bulk opportunity. Multiple store owners (Pilar's Wellness Collective, Secrets of the Garden) have independently asked about bulk cacao tea and flagged they cannot find suppliers. This may be a larger wedge than ceremonial cacao for some regions.' That points to a B2B-bulk segment with demonstrated inbound demand and no conversion machinery - which sits precisely at the tension in question (2).
  
  (6) TENSION TO RESOLVE: Jerry's SKU-simplification advice and the B2B-bulk question pull against each other. A single-line SKU story is the right answer for DTC and retail-shelf clarity; bulk-for-manufacturers is by definition NOT one line and not one SKU. Recommend deciding the PRIMARY model first, then simplifying to that model's one line - otherwise the SKU list gets collapsed in a way that strands the bulk lane, or preserved in a way that keeps the shelf story muddy.
- Type: Time (Minutes)
--------
